en: The *Śamīra Sūtra*, translated anonymously and appended to the *Records of the Three Qin*.
Formerly, there was a young boy named Śamīra. He was seven years of age and possessed a disposition that delighted in the Way and its virtue.
He followed a certain śramaṇa as his disciple;
dwelling in the mountains, he performed whatever tasks his teacher assigned him,
reciting and contemplating the sūtras and the Dharma with a mind free from indolence.
By the time he was eight years old, he attained arhatship.
His eye of the Way could see through all things with boundless clarity;
his ears could hear with penetrating acuity, such that all the good and evil deeds performed in the heavens above and the world below were heard by him entirely.
The body is able to fly, reaching wherever it intends;
it can divide a single body into ten thousand bodies;
manifesting transformations with sovereign ease, there is nothing it cannot do.
He knew his own past lives and the origins from which he had come; he fully understood all beings, both human and non-human, including those that crawl and wriggle.
While sitting, he beheld his past lives and saw that he had been the son of five mothers, whereupon he laughed to himself.
Then the teacher looked back and addressed the śrāmaṇera Rāhula:
"What are you laughing at?
There are no songs or dances here in the mountains; are you mocking me?"
The śrāmaṇera said: "I do not dare to laugh at my teacher; rather, I laugh at myself!

A single spirit receives a body and becomes the child of five mothers. These five mothers weep and wail for me day and night; their grief and anguish are so profound that they cannot be restrained. They constantly speak of and think of me, never once forgetting."
Reflecting upon myself alone, yet grieving for the sake of five families, I laughed at this; yet I did not dare to laugh at my teacher.
"When I was a child of the First Mother, there was a neighbor who also gave birth to a son on the same day as mine."
"After I have died, he will go out and come in, and walk about, at the same times as I did.
When his mother saw him, she said:
"Alas, my son! Even while at home, his going out, coming in, and walking about are just like this!"
Filled with sorrow and grief, his tears fell like rain.
"When I was her child under my second mother, I died prematurely at an early age.
When my mother saw others nursing their infants, she would think of nursing me; thus, she was moved by the memory of me and filled with grief."
"When I was a son to my third mother, I was ten years old when my life ended.
When my mother was eating her meal, she wept with grief, saying:
'If my son were here, I would eat together with him;'"
"Abandoning me to die, you leave me to eat alone?
She choked with sobs and called out to Heaven, lamenting and longing for her son:
"When I was your son as your fourth mother, my fate was thin and I died first."
When my mother saw that we had all married wives at the same time through the efforts of matchmakers, she thought of us with sorrow and said:
"Now that these sons of mine are here, they too shall take wives!"
"What offense have I committed that you should kill my son?
"When I was his son under my fifth mother, I was seven years old when I took pleasure in the Way and left home;
I abandoned my mother to follow a teacher, entering the mountains to seek the Way."
With single-minded concentration in meditation, he attained the path of Arhatship.
His mother wept day after day, thinking of him:
"I gave birth to an only son who followed a teacher to study the Way; I do not know where he is?"
"Are hunger, thirst, cold, and heat now death or life?
Thereupon, the five mothers gathered in one place; each was filled with sorrow, thinking of their sons, and they wept together against one another, unable to restrain themselves.

I am a single soul that has passed through the wombs of five mothers in succession to become their child; by depending upon my two parents, I have received form and become a human being, yet I have caused those five mothers to weep and go mad, each grieving for me so intensely that they even wished to take their own lives—this is why I laugh!

"I contemplate the world: the causes and conditions of the net of desire, the transgressions and blessings of birth and death, and the roots of karmic action—whereby evil leads to entry into hell and virtuous conduct results in rebirth in heaven."
Fearing the sufferings of the world, I left my home to enter the mountains;
through diligent application and meditative concentration, I attained the Way and ascended as an immortal.

Beholding the places of suffering for hungry ghosts, those in hell, and animals, I felt terror on their behalf; I took pity on my five mothers who could not liberate themselves and were further anxious for my own person.
That which I have sought, may my practice accord with my words; may I forever leave birth and death behind, sever the roots of the body, and, like one who does not sow seeds, attain Nirvana.
After the Venerable Suvīra had finished speaking, he flew up into the air.
*Śrāmaṇeraka-sūtra*
